_what: NR4A3 fusion junctions recovered from DEPOSITED SEQUENCE RECORDS — the survey that lit-targets-aso-breakpoint-census.json names as missing.
_why: That census states in its own words: 'Not a survey of sequence databases. Everything above except the TCF12 deposit comes from papers; the deposit came from NCBI elink, and no comparable sweep of the other partners' deposits has been read into this file.' This is that sweep.
_cost: $0 — NCBI E-utilities on a free GitHub Actions runner (run 31890517984, 9m03s).
_how_the_exon_pair_is_derived: By matching each deposit's OWN nucleotide sequence against this repository's committed transcript models (aso-premrna-sequences.json), requiring 16 nt exact on EACH side of the seam. Never read off a title.
_what_this_is_not: NOT a prevalence measurement. Deposit counts are not tumour counts: what gets cloned and deposited is chosen, not sampled.
NOT a claim any junction is druggable.
NOT independent patients wherever several records share an originating group or patent family.
\u2b50_the_alias_finding: Three of the four TAF15 deposits are titled with RETIRED symbols — 'hTAFII68-CHN' (AF162670.1), 'RBP56/CHN' (AJ243810.1), 'TAF2N-TEC' (AJ245932.1). None contains the string 'NR4A3' or 'TAF15'. A sweep using current gene symbols would have returned none of them. The alias table is the instrument.

TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.\u2b50 status: NEW TO THIS REPOSITORY — the census carried NO exon-resolved TFG breakpoint at all (TFG appears in that file only inside its search string).
TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.\u26a0 evidence_grade: ONE primary GenBank mRNA (AY532911.1, 'TFG-NR4A3 fusion protein, partial cds') plus FOUR Korean patent sequences that agree on the identical seam. The patent records are one family from one group — they are CORROBORATION OF A SEQUENCE, NOT four independent patients. No PMID is attached to any of the five.
TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.\u26d4 not_a_frequency: Nothing here says what fraction of TFG-rearranged EMC breaks at exon 7.

TAF15_e6__NR4A3_e3.status: CONFIRMED at sequence level — the census had this from papers (k=3/3); these are the underlying deposits.
TAF15_e6__NR4A3_e3.\u26d4 WHAT IT DOES NOT DO \u2014 READ T: It does NOT bound the intron-2 fraction and must not be read as reassurance about the 3/3 pricing. ASCERTAINMENT: all three primary deposits are from 1999–2000. The intron-2 acceptor was not described until 2019 (PMID 31020999). Cloning of that era used primers anchored in NR4A3 EXON 3, which STRUCTURALLY CANNOT recover an intron-2 junction — so zero intron-2 deposits is the EXPECTED result whether or not the variant is common. The absence carries essentially no evidence. The census's named risk on the TAF15 arm stands unchanged.

EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.status: CONFIRMED at sequence level — census had k=1/20 from papers; this is an independent deposited patient sequence.
EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.\u26a0 anchor_note: The EWSR1 side of this 175 nt record contributes only ~40 nt, so the assignment rests on a shorter donor block than the others (still ≥16 nt exact, the module's floor).
EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.bearing_on_the_3_unresolved_EWSR1_tumour: The census leaves 3 of 20 EWSR1 tumours unresolved and notes they are 'likely' type 2. This deposit confirms e7::e2 is a real recurrent junction in a DIFFERENT patient — it does NOT resolve those three, and 'likely' remains not a count.

TCF12_e5__NR4A3_e3.status: RE-FOUND INDEPENDENTLY — the known deposit, recovered blind by the sweep. Serves as the end-to-end positive control.

\u26d4 a_defect_in_my_own_classifier: classify_material() graded LG067227.1 and LG067228.1 as PATIENT_MATERIAL. That is WRONG. They are Korean patent filings ('Compositions for Preventing or Treating a Tumor Disorder Comprising TFG-TEC Protein Mutant'); the grader matched the word 'Tumor' in a patent title and there is no tissue_type or cell_line field to contradict it. The two sibling records DI433544.1/DI438966.1 were graded ENGINEERED_CONSTRUCT only because their titles happen to contain the token 'Construct'. Fix: treat a DI/LG/PAT accession prefix as a patent record and never grade it patient material. Until fixed, do not read the material field on any patent-prefixed accession.
what_this_changes: TFG gains its first exon-resolved breakpoint, so a TFG arm is designable in principle where before it was not.
Two existing census entries gain independent sequence-level support.
NOTHING about coverage percentages changes here — these are junction identities, not prevalences, and the partner denominators are untouched.
